title: performance canary: adaptive KV hysteresis + automated regression detection and rollout guards
author: Jordan Lee
description: Motivation: We've seen a handful of subtle regressions that only surface in long-running, real-traffic canaries due to KV cache churn and transient latency spikes. This PR implements an adaptive hysteresis layer for the KV cache detector and wires automated regression detection into the rollout controller so rollouts pause automatically when throughput/latency regressions exceed configurable thresholds. Changes include a new adaptive hysteresis algorithm, instrumentation for canary metrics, CI integration, and docs. Checklist: - [x] Implement adaptive hysteresis algorithm - [x] Integrate detector with rollout controller and canary jobs - [x] Add unit + integration tests - [x] Update Helm values and deployment manifests - [x] Add docs and release notes - [x] Smoke-tested on staging via perf-canary job See also: Linear ENG-3245 (canary auto-detect iterations) and ENG-4132 (rollout guard integration). Related PRs: pr-2143, pr-91234 for prior detector iterations.

review_comments: Ava Chen: Nice work — the hysteresis algorithm looks sane, but we should ensure the default window sizes are conservative. Can we add a config knob to tune sensitivity per-customer?
Jordan Lee: Added sensitivity config and per-customer override (see Helm values). Default window is 5 minutes with exponential backoff; updated docs.

Jordan Lee: Added dashboard docs and a suppression-count alert in observability queries. Thanks for the review!
release_notes: Introduce adaptive KV hysteresis for perf canaries and automated rollback/pausing rollout guards when latency/throughput regressions are detected. Added Helm knobs to tune sensitivity per deployment. Improves canary stability and reduces noisy rollouts.
notes_for_oncall: If canary rollouts start frequently pausing, check canary.hysteresis.suppression_count and canary.detector.latency_regressions; increase sensitivity or temporarily disable auto-pause via Helm override rollout.auto_pause=false.
egress_summary: No external data exfiltration. New metrics emitted to internal metrics namespace 'canary.'
migration_instructions: Helm chart bump required for perf-canary deployment; set perfCanary.controller.image to new tag. Backwards compatible with previous controller; migration is safe to apply as a rolling update.
testing_steps: 1) Deploy to staging with perf-canary enabled. 2) Run synthetic traffic that increases KV misses and observe detector metrics. 3) Introduce a controlled latency regression and verify the rollout controller pauses. 4) Confirm metrics emitted: canary.hysteresis.window, canary.detector.latency_regressions, canary.rollout.paused_count.

additional_context: This builds on prior detector improvements (see pr-2143 and pr-91234). The adaptive hysteresis uses a small state machine with exponential backoff to avoid flip-flopping on noisy signals and a suppression counter to avoid alert storms. We intentionally conservative default thresholds but provide per-customer tuning to handle high-throughput workloads.
